title: TypeScript SDK: streaming contract compatibility & ergonomic conversion guide
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: produce a concrete, implementation-ready guide and a small compatibility utility library for TypeScript SDK consumers that need first-class conversions and composability between Node-style AsyncIterator-based token streams and Web Streams (ReadableStream) used across browser and Deno runtimes.

Background: teams and customers report friction when integrating Redwood’s streaming SDK with heterogeneous runtimes: some libraries and frameworks prefer Node AsyncIterator consumption patterns, others favor Web Streams for DOM/Fetch pipeline compatibility. Existing partial adapters live in internal PRs but lack a canonical contract, test suite, and clear semantics around backpressure, cancellation propagation, resumability, and error mapping. Without a single source of truth, customers implement brittle adapters that leak resources or drop tokens.

Scope:
- Define the canonical runtime contract for the SDK’s streaming responses (token and chunk shape, end-of-stream semantics, error / status propagation).
- Implement a small utilities package (ts-sdk-stream-utils) exporting: asyncIteratorToReadableStream, readableStreamToAsyncIterator, streamWithBackpressureProxy, and a cancelPropagationShim.
- Document edge cases: cancellation during in-flight tokens, transform stream usage, binary token payloads, partial-frame truncation, and resumable continuation hints.
- Provide a matrix of recommended converters per environment (Node 18+, Cloudflare Workers, Deno, Browser) with polyfill guidance.
- Add unit + integration tests that run in Node and a headless browser (Puppeteer) to validate backpressure and close semantics.
- Provide example snippets for SDK README and Console docs.

Non-goals: full rewrite of the SDK streaming runtime or changing the wire protocol. This is compatibility and ergonomics tooling only.

Acceptance criteria:
1) A design doc describing the streaming contract merged to Confluence and linked from the repo.
2) Utilities package implemented with public API and types that compile under strict TS settings.
3) End-to-end tests verifying: a) consumer cancellation is forwarded to the runtime; b) backpressure from ReadableStream applies back to generator pull pace; c) errors on the producing side surface to both iterator and stream consumers consistently.
4) Migration guide + three short examples (Node async iteration, browser fetch + pipeline, and transform-stream-based aggregator).
5) Bench notes: conversion overhead <= 5% token latency at 512 token windows in microbench harness.

Implementation notes / proposals:
- Define TokenEnvelope { text: string, delta?: boolean, done?: boolean } as the canonical JS shape for stream items. Use strict typings and export it.
- For readableStreamToAsyncIterator: use getReader() where available, respect read() backpressure, and yield items as Promises that resolve in order. Ensure errors from reader.read() reject iterator next().
- For asyncIteratorToReadableStream: implement a ReadableStream with an underlying pull controller that calls iterator.next(). Convert iterator return() calls into controller.close(). If iterator provides a throw(), map to controller.error().
- Backpressure proxy: when converting between systems that do not share a native backpressure signal (e.g., an underlying SDK push-based stream), implement a bounded queue with promises to apply write wait. Provide knobs for queueSize and dropStrategy (backpressure | drop-oldest | drop-newest) and default to backpressure.
- Cancellation: ensure iterator.return() and reader.cancel() both call a normalized cancel hook on the SDK response object (exported symbol) so SDK runtime can release KV cache and GPU handles.

Testing approach:
- Unit tests for each util under ts-jest and a separate runner that executes Node and a headless Chromium instance to validate ReadableStream semantics in the browser.
- Create a synthetic producer that emits tokens at configurable pace; assert consumer backpressure affects producer rate when using proxy.
- Add tests for partial frame handling by simulating chunked text frames.

Docs + Examples: three annotated examples (small runnable snippets) to be added to SDK README and a new page in Console docs: "Streaming interop patterns".

Risks & tradeoffs:
- Complexity: bridging two different runtime primitives inevitably introduces non-zero overhead. We aim to keep it minimal and provide opt-out paths when maximum throughput is required.
- Failure semantics: mapping exceptions and cancellation consistently across runtimes is subtle (e.g., reader.cancel() takes a reason in some runtimes). We will normalize to an { reason?: string } shape.

Rollout plan:
- Week 1 (design + PRs): design doc + types + initial tests.
- Week 2 (implementation): utils package and unit tests.
- Week 3 (integration): browser/NODE harness, docs, examples, and ship as minor release behind opt-in flag.

comments: 2025-02-19 - Aisha Patel: Kickoff meeting summary attached to the Confluence page. Decided to prefer explicit TokenEnvelope typing rather than raw strings to make downstream transforms easier.

2025-02-21 - Luca Moreno: Initial draft of asyncIteratorToReadableStream in PR #2042. Early tests show close semantics OK but need to handle iterator.throw() mapping to stream.error() — adding test case.

2025-02-24 - Priya Shah (reviewer): Left review comments: ensure cancelPropagationShim calls SDK response.cancel() and that the shim is unit-tested for idempotence. Also requested an accessibility note for browser examples (avoid long-running CPU loops in main thread).
2025-02-26 - Luca Moreno: Implemented bounded queue with backpressure default. Microbench shows ~2.1% median additional latency at 512 tokens. Pushed updated tests and bench logs to PR.

2025-03-01 - Security (James O): Quick review — no secrets are leaked by conversion utilities. Suggested adding a note about not serializing KMS-protected payloads via toString() in examples. Marked security_review_required=false.

2025-03-02 - Aisha Patel: Merging docs to Confluence. Preparing migration notes for SDK README. Planning to toggle opt-in flag for the release and collect telemetry for two weeks before defaulting on in sdk-2025.04.
